questions.q: What does "shifting left" mean in the context of a software delivery timeline?
options: Moving security checks earlier in the SDLC — into the editor, commit, and build stages — instead of relying on one review right before release
Replacing the development team with a dedicated security team
Moving the production deployment earlier in the calendar year
Running all security checks only after a customer reports an issue
questions.explain: Shifting left means moving security checks earlier on the SDLC timeline — into the editor, pre-commit hooks, and CI — rather than gating everything on a single pre-release review.

questions.q: Why did the old model of "one security review right before release" break down as release cadence increased?
options: It never worked, even with infrequent releases
Security reviews became illegal under modern compliance rules
With multiple releases a day, there's no single convenient pre-release moment to gate everything on, and a review at the end makes every release late
Modern applications no longer contain vulnerabilities
questions.explain: The lesson explains that frequent releases remove the single 'before release' moment the old model depended on, turning an end-of-pipeline review into a bottleneck.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what typically has to happen when a vulnerability is found in production rather than in code review?
options: Nothing changes — the fix process is identical regardless of where it's found
It becomes an incident: assessing possible exploitation, preparing an emergency hotfix, possibly rolling back unrelated work, and possibly notifying customers or regulators
The original developer is immediately fired
The vulnerability is automatically patched by the CI pipeline with no human involvement
questions.explain: The lesson walks through how a production finding escalates into an incident involving assessment, emergency hotfix approval, possible rollback, and possible disclosure — far more than a code-review fix requires.

questions.q: What is a pre-commit hook, as described in this lesson?
options: A manual penetration test scheduled before a major release
A production monitoring dashboard
A legal agreement developers sign before contributing code
A check that runs locally before a commit is created, catching issues before they reach source control
questions.explain: A pre-commit hook runs locally, before a commit is even created, letting issues be caught before they reach source control at all.

questions.q: What does the lesson say this chapter builds toward after this lesson?
options: SAST and dependency scanning (Lesson 22), DAST and container image scanning (Lesson 23), then setting security gates (Lesson 24)
A complete replacement of Python automation with manual security reviews
Moving directly to incident response without covering any build-pipeline checks
A single, all-in-one scanner that replaces every other tool mentioned in the course
questions.explain: The lesson previews the chapter's progression: static checks (SAST, dependency scanning) in Lesson 22, dynamic and container checks in Lesson 23, and gate design in Lesson 24.
